clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old female with intellectual disability and a history of seizures, on Carbamazepine and Phenobarbital, presented with dental caries and tooth pain. She also had wart-like facial lesions since age 7, described as distributed in a butterfly pattern over the face, especially involving the nose. Brain MRI revealed several cortical and subcortical tubers, and subependymal glial nodules. The MRI also showed no evidence of giant cell astrocytomas or aneurysm. Considering the patient's history of tuberous sclerosis, the most probable diagnosis was cortical and subcortical glioneuronal tubers, with some subependymal glial nodules also present.
